clue.text: Back, like a bird

parts.note: as means like, in the sense 'as a bird'
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of something both behind and bird-like.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'like a bird' as two pieces: 'like' is AS and 'a bird' is TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for at or towards the rear of a ship, so it means back.

clue.text: Pressure Senator Thurmond about northern tabloid on the rise

indicators.note: about means around, so the first name wraps the other letters

parts.note: Strom Thurmond was a long-serving US senator from South Carolina

indicators.note: in a down answer, on the rise means read upwards, so the word for tabloid is reversed

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a cheap newspaper, a tabloid

explanation.surface: A senator surrounded by a gossip paper from up north whose circulation is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rise' sounds like sales going up, but in a down answer it means read upwards, so the tabloid gives GAR. 'About' wraps the senator's first name around N and GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To strong-arm someone is to coerce them with force or threats, that is to put pressure on them.

clue.text: Marine sex-change inspectors

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier in the Marines undergoing a sex change, oddly linked to inspectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex-change' reads as one compound, but only 'sex' is fodder; 'change' is the anagram signal for MARINE and SEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners are people who inspect or test, so they are inspectors by another name.

clue.text: Strangely, Saturn contains a tiny plant that's a source of energy

indicators.note: contains means the shuffled letters hold another piece inside them
strangely suggests something oddly arranged, so the letters of the planet's name are mixed

parts.note: an alga is a simple, often microscopic plant

explanation.surface: A planetary science aside: Saturn holds some minute plant that might fuel things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' scrambles the planet to NATURS and 'contains' puts the alga inside it, between the R and the S. The answer runs on into the three-letter light at 15.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural gas, mainly methane, is a fossil fuel burned to heat homes and generate electricity.

clue.text: Curtailed talk about Frisbee at the Olympics?

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter of the word for talk about is dropped

parts.note: to discuss something is to talk about it

explanation.surface: A joke about a short chat on what a frisbee would be called in Olympic competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' docks the tail of DISCUSS, leaving one S at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus is the flat disc thrown in Olympic athletics, a heavyweight relative of the Frisbee, hence the question mark.

clue.text: French writer in the grip of sordid erotica

indicators.note: held in the grip of other words, so the answer is hidden across them

parts.note: the end of sordid and the start of erotica together spell the name

explanation.surface: A French author caught up in seedy pornography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the grip of' says the name is held inside 'sordid erotica', across the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was an 18th-century French philosopher and novelist who edited the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: See 16
Before hunt, illuminate innards

indicators.note: innards are what is inside, so the answer lies inside the words that come before

parts.note: the last two letters of hunt and the first three of illuminate run together

explanation.surface: A hunting party lighting its lamps before setting off, with talk of guts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innards' sounds like the offal of the hunt; it means the letters are inside 'hunt, illuminate', across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Until is a preposition meaning up to the time of, used as before is in 'wait until noon'.

clue.text: Matt Drudge, finally taken in by president, laid out…

indicators.note: something taken in by a word sits inside it, so these letters go within the president's name

parts.note: Gerald Ford was the 38th US president

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word, here Drudge

parts.note: last letter of Drudge

explanation.surface: The online gossip Matt Drudge is welcomed into a president's circle and set out in print.
explanation.walkthrough: Matt Drudge runs a US news aggregator site; 'finally' takes only the last letter of his surname, and 'taken in by' puts it with his whole first name inside Gerald Ford's surname. The ellipsis carries 'laid out' on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that has been formatted has been arranged on the page, which is to say laid out.

clue.text: Skip ahead and refuse to eat, in solidarity with Cleaver

parts.note: to fast is to go without food
to be for something is to support it
Ward Cleaver is the father in the US sitcom Leave It to Beaver

explanation.surface: A hunger strike in support of a protester named Cleaver, with a jump ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleaver evokes Eldridge Cleaver the Black Panther, which suits the hunger strike, but the piece is Ward Cleaver, the sitcom dad.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast-forward is to wind a recording on quickly, or more loosely to skip ahead in time.

clue.text: …the letters needed for the last name of a constructor of crosswords about vision

indicators.note: the letters needed for a name are just its set of letters, free to be laid out in any order, as the previous clue's ending says

parts.words: the last name of a constructor of crosswords
parts.note: Henri Picciotto, co-setter of this very puzzle; his surname uses only five different letters, P, I, C, O and T

explanation.surface: The setter talks about the letters in a fellow crossword maker's surname, with a nod to sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to the previous clue's 'laid out'. 'The letters needed for' PICCIOTTO, surname of one of this puzzle's setters, are just P, I, C, O and T, each once; laid out, they give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective meaning relating to the eye or to sight, so it stands for about vision.

clue.text: Disaster: hipster with a verse

parts.note: cat is jazz-age slang for a cool person, a hipster
a strophe is a stanza, a section of verse

explanation.surface: Calamity: a trendy type reciting poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: A strophe is a stanza of a poem, from Greek choral odes.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is an event causing great damage or suffering, a synonym for disaster.

clue.text: More cheerful, and more like a devout Muslim?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: more Sunni, a comparative formed playfully from the branch of Islam

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense treats Sunni, the largest branch of Islam, as if it took -er; the question mark flags the made-up comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunnier disposition is a happier one, and the word also puns on Sunni, the main branch of Islam.

clue.text: Horrid girl, ten, with a little curl

indicators.note: horrid suggests something messed up, so the letters of the following words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A beastly ten-year-old girl twirling a lock of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrid' looks like a description of the girl, but it is the signal to rearrange GIRL and TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a small spiral lock of hair, which is exactly a little curl.

clue.text: Jack Fitzgerald Kennedy is whipped

parts.note: a jack is a small flag flown on a ship
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer
Ted Kennedy, the long-serving Massachusetts senator

explanation.surface: A man called Jack Fitzgerald Kennedy, echoing JFK, is said to have been flogged.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of names mimics John Fitzgerald Kennedy, but each name is a separate piece: Jack is a flag, and the other two give the first names of Ella Fitzgerald and Ted Kennedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To flagellate is to flog, so flagellated is a formal synonym for whipped.

clue.text: San Diego's shifting assessments

indicators.note: shifting means moving around, so the letters of the city's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Californian city's changing evaluations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifting' rearranges the letters, and the S of the possessive is part of the fodder: SANDIEGOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnoses are a doctor's judgements of what is wrong, that is medical assessments.

clue.text: See 4
Outages he repaired in groundskeeper's dwelling, possibly

indicators.note: repaired means fixed by putting back together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A man fixes power cuts in the groundsman's cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repaired' sounds like fixing the outages; it rearranges OUTAGES and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatehouse is a lodge at an estate entrance, often the home of a groundsman, hence the 'possibly'.

clue.text: Batter clipped holiday noise-maker

parts.note: to ram something is to batter it
shorn means clipped, as a sheep's fleece is

explanation.surface: Cake batter cut short, oddly paired with a festive noise-making toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter clipped' looks like a mixture docked of a letter, but both words are pieces: RAM and SHORN. A ram's horn, the shofar, is blown at the Jewish New Year, Rosh Hashanah.
explanation.definitionFit: The shofar is a trumpet made from a ram's horn and sounded on the High Holy Days, so it is a festival noise-maker.

clue.text: Blow up air mattress — that'll get you some exercise

indicators.note: to blow up is to explode, which scatters the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Instructions to inflate an air mattress, with the joke that the pumping is a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' reads as inflating the mattress, but it signals that AIR and MATTRESS explode into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A StairMaster is a stair-climbing gym machine, a piece of equipment built to give you exercise.

clue.text: A black cat, perhaps, with head stuffed inside belly

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is pushed one place inside the phrase, so it swaps with the letter after it

parts.note: a black cat crossing your path is supposed to be a bad omen

explanation.surface: A dark-furred cat with its head squashed into a stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A black cat, perhaps' is BAD OMEN. 'With head stuffed inside' moves its first letter, B, in behind the A, so BA becomes AB.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the part of the body containing the stomach and guts, the belly.

clue.text: Nineteenth-century style: checkered green with corduroy fringes

indicators.note: checkered suggests a mixed-up pattern, so these letters are rearranged
the fringes of a word are its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of corduroy

explanation.surface: Describing a fabric pattern: green checks with corduroy edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringes' gives CY, the outer letters of corduroy; 'checkered' looks like part of the fabric description, but it signals the anagram of GREEN with CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Regency style is the elegant British design and architecture of the period around 1811 to 1820.

clue.text: Praise piece of software backed up twofold

parts.note: an app is an application, a piece of software

indicators.note: backed up means sent backwards, so the word for twofold is reversed

parts.note: dual means twofold, having two parts

explanation.surface: Commending a program that has been saved twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed up' looks like computer jargon for a saved copy; here it means the word for twofold is written backwards, giving LAUD, itself a word for praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to clap, and by extension to commend or express approval.

clue.text: Groom 'em?

parts.note: the letter M comes just before N in the alphabet, so it is pre-N

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as PRE-EN, before N: the letter that comes before N is M, spelt out as 'em'.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen is to groom oneself carefully, as a bird does with its feathers.

clue.text: Trim both sides of pattern for walkway

indicators.note: trimming both sides cuts off the first and last letters of the word for pattern

parts.note: paisley is a teardrop-shaped fabric pattern

explanation.surface: Cutting the edges off a fabric design to make a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pattern' has to become the specific design PAISLEY before 'Trim both sides of' cuts away its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats or shelves, a walkway.

clue.text: Military aircraft pushing violently

indicators.note: violently suggests a forceful shake-up of the word that comes before it

explanation.surface: A warplane forcing its way through.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the single word before 'violently': the seven letters of PUSHING rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunship is a heavily armed helicopter or plane used for ground attack.

clue.text: The most undesirable part of departmental leadership: rules

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so leadership picks the opening letter of departmental

parts.note: first letter of departmental
regs is a short form of regulations, that is rules

explanation.surface: Office grumbling: the worst thing about the bosses is their rulebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departmental leadership' reads like the management; it is just the D at the head of 'departmental'. REGS is informal shorthand for regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment at the bottom of a drink, and figuratively the least valued portion of anything.

clue.text: Brand-new attitude — what you'd need to serve lamb

definitions.text: what you'd need to serve lamb

parts.note: in mint condition means brand-new
sauce is cheek or impudence, that is attitude

explanation.surface: A fresh outlook, then a turn to dinner and roast lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Mint sauce is the traditional British accompaniment to roast lamb. 'Attitude' means cheekiness, which British English calls sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint sauce, chopped mint in vinegar and sugar, is the classic condiment served alongside roast lamb.

clue.text: Bury nurse, at first, with doctor

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it, nurse

parts.note: first letter of nurse

explanation.surface: A hospital scene: burying a nurse alongside a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' tempts as an anagram signal, but it is the definition; 'at first' acts on 'nurse'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US an intern is a junior hospital physician in the first year after medical school.

clue.text: Sycophants smuggle sulfur into Middle Eastern country

indicators.note: to smuggle something is to slip it in, so one piece goes inside another
into names the container, the Middle Eastern country

parts.note: Yemen is a country on the Arabian peninsula
S is the chemical symbol for sulfur

explanation.surface: Flatterers running contraband chemicals into the Arabian peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men agree with whatever a superior says, which is the behaviour of sycophants.
